transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-07-21 15:30 PT — duration 58m
Attendees: Evelyn Cho (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Dana Morales (Archipelago Head of Platform), Ravi Singh (SRE), Lina Park (Product Lead)

Summary:
Quick POC scoping to agree workload characterization for a small pilot. Archipelago has a bimodal traffic pattern (morning batch ingestion + evening interactive peak), heavy token asymmetry (short prompts, long generated docs for reports), and strict tail-latency targets during business hours. Discussed replay, benchmarks, and success criteria. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics discussed:
- Bimodal QPS (batch vs interactive) and concurrency mapping
- Input/output token distribution and skew impact on KV cache and batching
- Tail latency SLOs and acceptable p95/p99 targets for both modes
- Benchmark design: replay harness, synthetic bursts, steady-state runs
- Timeline and artifacts: sample logs, security docs, run windows

00:00 Evelyn: Okay, thanks everyone for joining. I think we have about an hour, we'll go through your traffic shape, success criteria, and then Marcus will sketch a benchmark plan.
00:18 Dana: Yeah thanks, Evelyn. Real quick context — Archipelago runs an internal reporting assistant. Nightly batch ingest triggers a generation job that creates multi-page reports (so long outputs), then during day we have an interactive assistant where prompts are short but latency is king.
00:38 Ravi: To add, we see two clear peaks: a 2am batch flood where we can tolerate slightly higher latency, and a 10am–11am interactive peak where sub-200ms for p95 is preferred.
00:55 Marcus: Got it. When you say "multi-page reports" — what are we talking about in tokens? 2k outputs, 4k outputs?
01:05 Dana: Usually between 1.5k to 3.5k output tokens. Inputs are small, like 50–150 tokens. So there's a big asymmetry.
01:20 Evelyn: Perfect, that asymmetry drives a different resource profile. We'll want to test two benchmark modes: high-throughput long-output mode (batch) and low-latency short-output mode (interactive).
01:36 Lina: For success criteria — product wants interactive p95 < 200ms, p99 < 400ms during business hours. For batch we want throughput to finish within our nightly window and 99th token latency relaxed to 1.5s. Cost per generated document is also a gating metric; we'd like a delta vs current infra under 20%.
01:58 Marcus: Note — p95/p99 measured at the HTTP response end-to-end including prefix cache hit/miss, KV cache warm/cold scenarios. We should capture both cold-start and steady-state.
02:15 Ravi: We do have a prefix cache at the app layer right now, but it's fairly coarse. Curious how Redwood's automatic prefix/KV caching might help reduce cost and tail.
02:28 Marcus: Redwood's runtime supports KV cache reuse across requests when the conversation sharding aligns — but for long outputs the KV grows large. We'll want to measure memory footprint and memory eviction behavior under your max sequence lengths.
02:45 Evelyn: For the POC we recommend two runs: 1) Replay 48h of production traffic (anonymized) to capture real QPS/concurrency and token mix. 2) Controlled synthetic burst tests to stress the tail and confirm autoscale/burst policies.
03:03 Dana: We can provide logs but need to scrub personal data. Is there a template for what you need?
03:10 Evelyn: Yes, we'll send a CSV template — timestamp, request_id, user_tier, input_tokens, output_tokens_estimate, route. Marcus will also share a sample s3 layout for the replay harness.
03:23 Marcus: On the harness: plan is k6 + a prompt feeder that streams the request body and measures streaming latencies where applicable. We'll run 3 phases: warmup, steady-state, and burst windows (10–20x short spikes).
03:39 Lina: How do you simulate the token expansion? Long outputs are generated token-by-token, so you need to mirror generation pacing.
03:47 Marcus: We will — for long outputs we'll emulate the model's per-token generation timing by replaying the KV growth and using a token-level timeline. It's not perfect but gives realistic runtime behavior.
03:58 Ravi: Good. About concurrency — our interactive traffic is highly concurrent from the web frontend: dozens to low hundreds concurrent sessions depending on campaign. Our current telemetry shows typical concurrency ~120 during midday peak, QPS around 75 but with many multi-turn sessions.
04:18 Marcus: Important distinction: QPS and concurrency are different levers. For cost mapping we need both the instantaneous token throughput (tokens/sec) and simultaneous in-flight requests (# concurrent). We'll capture both during replay.
04:34 Evelyn: On the platform side, you'll want to test both Hosted (our managed API) and Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) during the POC. Dedicated gives more consistent p99 but has commit cost; hosted shows autoscale behavior. We can provide both for the pilot.
04:52 Dana: Security — we'll need SOC2 docs, SSO/SAML integration notes, and confirmation about KMS for key management. Also audit logs and model residency controls (can't leave EU region for some customers).
05:07 Evelyn: We'll attach our security pack. We support customer KMS integrations for Private deployments and can run the pilot in your preferred region where available.
05:15 Lina: For quality gating — our product team will sample outputs for a set of 120 prompts; we need to ensure no regression in output fidelity. How do we capture that?
05:27 Marcus: We can run a diff/eval harness that runs your prompt set against baseline model and Redwood-served model and compute rouge/bert scores or custom quality heuristics you supply. We'll also keep human review as part of the POC.
05:40 Ravi: What's the expected timeline? We need to move quickly, two-weeks to a month ideally.
05:45 Evelyn: Proposed timeline: Day 0–3: exchange artifacts and access; Day 4–10: run replay + initial benchmarks; Day 11–14: review results and tune autoscale/batching; Week 3–4: optional extended runs and cost modeling. So roughly a 2–4 week pilot depending on iterations.
06:03 Marcus: For metrics we'll produce: p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, memory footprint, and quality deltas per prompt set.
06:18 Dana: Can you show an example report? A concise spreadsheet with sections for interactive vs batch, and per-route breakdown would be helpful.
06:26 Evelyn: We'll send a sample report format. It has sections for traffic surface (QPS, concurrency), token distribution histograms, tail-latency quantiles, and cost sensitivity analysis.
06:36 Lina: A few clarifying questions — 1) If we run Dedicated, how do rollouts work? 2) If traffic has sudden geo spikes, what's routing?
06:44 Marcus: 1) Dedicated is pinned capacity; you can pin model versions and rollouts via canary A/B. 2) Smart routing can route by region or latency policy; for POC we'll keep routing simple to focus on performance.
06:55 Ravi: We saw references to quantization in your docs — is that something we'll test?
07:00 Marcus: Yes, Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles. For POC we'll run baseline FP16/INT8-ish profiles where supported and measure quality vs cost. We'll be explicit about model variants.
07:12 Dana: About observability — we need request level traces, token-level cost attribution, and per-route dashboards.
07:19 Evelyn: Redwood Console exposes per-route token/latency breakdowns and traces. We'll enable a trial window for you to view live dashboards during the replay.
07:28 Lina: Any gotchas?
07:30 Marcus: A few: 1) Token asymmetry can make batching less effective — long outputs tend to serialize and block batching windows. 2) KV cache size and eviction will be key for long outputs — we need memory profiling. 3) Cold-starts for GPUs when autoscaling from zero can add to tail. We'll include tests to quantify each.
07:54 Ravi: For measurement accuracy, we want to measure from gateway to response—so we'll instrument both client and server sides and include clock sync notes in the template.
08:05 Evelyn: Great. Let's recap next steps. We'll send the benchmark template and replay harness instructions, Marcus will prepare the harness and do a smoke run, Archipelago will provide anonymized logs, and Lina will confirm the 120 prompt evaluation set.
08:23 Dana: Sounds good; one more, can you include a cost estimate for both Hosted and Dedicated for our mid-sized traffic?
08:29 Evelyn: Yes, we'll include a cost ballpark that includes reserved commit assumptions for Dedicated and an autoscale scenario for Hosted.
08:36 Lina: Ok thanks everyone. We'll look for the email and aim to have the logs to you by Thursday.
08:42 Evelyn: Thanks all — we'll follow up with calendar invites.

Action items/owners (verbatim as recorded):
- Evelyn: Send benchmark template, S3 layout, security pack (due 2025-07-24)

End of transcript.
